as_told.title: A chess champion's moves made themselves before a tournament, blamed on aliens

plain: This story is about a famous chess player, Vasily Smyslov, in a hotel room in Germany in the 1970s, in 1972 or 1974. Kiran Ilum Xenov, a man introduced on a podcast as the president of a Russian republic, tells it to the host, Jesse Michels, passing on what he says he heard. He names Smyslov's wife, Nadezhda Smyslova, and the opponent Smyslov was about to face, a player named Robert Hübner. According to Xenov, as Smyslov worked through his moves before the match, you could say an alien appeared right in front of him, and Xenov mentions Smyslov's own records of the game. Months later, Michels retells the story on another episode, crediting Xenov. In the host's version the player goes unnamed, the moves seemed to make themselves during a practice game, and the player put it down to some kind of alien help. If true, it would suggest that something non-human took a hand in a top chess game.
